QuestionStmt.S: Calculate work done if 1 mole of an ideal gas compressed isothermally and reversibly from 12 dm³ to 6 dm³ at 300 K. $[R = 8.314 \, \text{J} \cdot \text{K}^{-1} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}]$

Solution.S:
Given: $n = 1$ mol, $V_1 = 12$ dm³, $V_2 = 6$ dm³, $T = 300$ K, $R = 8.314$ J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

For isothermal reversible compression:

$$w = -nRT \ln \left( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right)$$

Substitute values:

$$w = -1 \times 8.314 \times 300 \times \ln \left( \frac{6}{12} \right)$$

$$w = -2494.2 \times \ln(0.5) = -2494.2 \times (-0.6931)$$

$$w = 1728.88 \text{ J} = 1.729 \text{ kJ}$$

Thus the correct option is A: 1.729 kJ.
